facts: The case involves an application filed by Dhariwal Tobaco Products Limited and Others under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
The application was dismissed by the High Court without entering into the merits of the matter.
The appellants argued that the High Court committed a serious error in rejecting their application without considering the merits of the case.
issues: Whether an application under Section 482 of the Code can be dismissed only on the premise that an alternative remedy of filing a revision application under Section 397 of the Code is available?
Whether the jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Code should not be used mechanically or routinely?
petitioner_arguments: The appellants argued that the High Court committed a serious error in rejecting their application without considering the merits of the case.
They contended that the issuance of summons was not an interlocutory order within the meaning of Section 397 of the Code.
respondent_arguments: The respondents contended that having regard to the conduct of the appellants, this Court should not exercise its extra-ordinary jurisdiction under Article 136 of the Constitution of India.
They argued that the power under Section 482 of the Code should not be used mechanically or routinely.
court_reasoning: The Court opined that the jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Code has to be exercised sparingly and only in exceptional cases.
It held that the issuance of summons is not an interlocutory order within the meaning of Section 397 of the Code.
It noted that the High Court's jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Code does not function either as a court of appeal or revision.
holding: The application filed by the appellants was allowed, and the proceedings were quashed.
